body: Ricoh India (Japanese parent held ~74%) admitted in Jul 2016 that its accounts were falsified; the estimated FY16 loss was Rs 1,123 cr (later Rs 1,118 cr) versus a company with a market cap of only a few thousand crore. A PwC forensic audit found unsupported out-of-books entries of Rs 66.7 cr in Q1FY16 alone that turned a Rs 64 cr loss into a Rs 2.7 cr profit; reports suggest the fraud began in FY14. SEBI barred 7 key managerial personnel in Feb 2018 and ordered a fuller forensic audit; the shares were suspended and the parent later recapitalised via NCLT, leaving minority holders with little. Visible flags: (1) the stock ran from ~Rs 100 to above Rs 1,000 in 2013-15 on a sudden revenue surge (services/'managed document' contracts) -- revenue growth far ahead of the parent and peers; (2) trade receivables and unbilled revenue rose faster than sales; (3) Q2FY16 results were delayed and the statutory auditor (BSR/KPMG) raised concerns; (4) thin free float (~26%) helped the run. Lesson: 'MNC parent' is not a governance guarantee for the Indian subsidiary; receivables growing faster than revenue plus delayed results is a classic pre-blowup combination (Beneish DSRI/TATA flags).

data.early_signals: revenue surge vs parent; receivables > revenue growth; delayed results; auditor queries; low float
data.lesson: MNC tag is not a shield; check DSO trend

title: Ricoh India accounting fraud (2016) -- MNC subsidiary is no shield
